name: MUI
best_for: Broad React product UI and enterprise-grade component coverage
risk: Strong default visual language; theme deeply rather than shipping the demo look

name: Ant Design
best_for: Dense business products, admin workflows, tables, forms, and internationalization
risk: Can make unrelated products look identical without a deliberate visual contract

name: Mantine
best_for: Flexible React applications needing accessible components and hooks
risk: Do not mix multiple overlapping component foundations

name: Chakra UI
best_for: Accessible composable React interfaces with design-token control
risk: Migration and recipe APIs must match the installed major version

name: shadcn/ui
best_for: Copy-owned React component foundations that can be art-directed in-source
risk: Default blocks are now an AI-template cliché; never ship them untransformed

name: Radix Primitives
best_for: Accessible behavior primitives with custom visual systems
risk: Primitives solve behavior, not information architecture or art direction

name: React Spectrum
best_for: Rigorous accessible interactions and internationalized React behavior
risk: Use the right layer: React Aria for custom visuals, Spectrum for Adobe styling

name: Ariakit
best_for: Accessible composable widgets with lower visual prescription
risk: Verify component stability and exact package version before migration

name: Floating UI
best_for: Robust popover, tooltip, menu, and floating element positioning
risk: Positioning engine is not a complete accessible component

name: TanStack Table
best_for: Headless data tables with product-owned rendering
risk: Complex tables still need deliberate density, mobile, and empty-state design

name: Apache ECharts
best_for: Broad interactive chart coverage and large datasets
risk: Theme and annotation require art direction; defaults look generic

name: D3
best_for: Custom data-driven visual explanation and unusual chart grammar
risk: Powerful primitives can cause reinvention; prefer higher-level charts for standard cases

name: Observable Plot
best_for: Concise expressive statistical graphics
risk: Interactive product dashboards may need a different event/state layer

name: Recharts
best_for: React-native composition of common product charts
risk: Accessibility and responsive labels need explicit work

name: Tiptap
best_for: Extensible ProseMirror-based rich text editing
risk: Open core boundaries and collaborative services require license/product review

name: Lexical
best_for: Composable performance-focused web editors
risk: Build only product-specific UX; do not recreate a complete editor ecosystem casually

name: Excalidraw
best_for: Hand-drawn collaborative diagrams and editable visual thinking
risk: Hand-drawn style is not appropriate for every formal or premium deliverable

name: tldraw
license_hint: Custom SDK license; inspect current terms
best_for: Extensible infinite canvas and whiteboard product foundations
risk: License/watermark/commercial terms are not equivalent to MIT

name: MapLibre GL JS
best_for: Open vector-tile maps and custom cartographic styling
risk: Tiles, geocoding, fonts, and data providers have separate cost/license constraints

name: Leaflet
best_for: Lightweight 2D maps and standard interaction
risk: Large vector datasets and advanced WebGL layers need another foundation

name: deck.gl
best_for: GPU geospatial layers, aggregation, trajectories, and 3D overlays
risk: Usually needs a basemap and explicit GPU performance budget

name: CesiumJS
best_for: Globe-scale 3D geospatial and 3D Tiles
risk: Heavy runtime; hosted Cesium ion terms differ from the open library

name: Motion
best_for: Product-state and layout animation in modern web apps
risk: Animation cannot compensate for weak hierarchy or excessive UI

name: GSAP
license_hint: GSAP standard/custom license; inspect current terms
best_for: Directed timelines, scroll choreography, SVG, canvas, and WebGL animation
risk: Source-visible is not the same as standard OSI open source; avoid gratuitous spectacle

name: Lenis
best_for: Controlled smooth scrolling and synchronized narrative experiences
risk: Must preserve keyboard, anchors, focus, native expectations, and reduced motion

name: Swup
best_for: Progressively enhanced page transitions with lifecycle hooks
risk: History, analytics, focus, and route-state restoration require explicit QA

name: AutoAnimate
best_for: Small list, reorder, expand, and layout continuity
risk: Not a substitute for a directed timeline; transforms can conflict with existing effects

name: Three.js
best_for: General WebGL 3D, product visualization, shaders, and creative sites
risk: Requires asset lifecycle, rendering, memory, accessibility, and performance governance

name: Babylon.js
best_for: Feature-rich web 3D engine, materials, tooling, physics, and XR
risk: Large engine footprint is unjustified for decorative background 3D

name: React Three Fiber
best_for: React-driven Three.js scene composition
risk: React componentization does not remove GPU/resource complexity

name: PixiJS
best_for: High-performance 2D canvas/WebGL rendering, games, and rich interaction
risk: Canvas content needs custom accessibility and responsive semantics

name: p5.js
license_hint: LGPL-2.1; inspect current license text for any later-version option
best_for: Creative coding, interactive art, education, and art-directed generative systems
risk: Never use a generative sketch as filler or call procedural output mature by default

name: PptxGenJS
best_for: Programmatic native PPTX assembly and repeatable slide generation
risk: Assembly code must populate an authored visual system rather than invent one from rectangles

name: Slidev
best_for: HTML/Vue/Markdown presentations with motion and developer-friendly reproducibility
risk: PPTX export/editability and offline target-viewer fidelity require a separate delivery strategy

name: Marp CLI
best_for: Markdown-first decks and reliable HTML/PDF/PPTX-like export pipelines
risk: Theme constraints can limit high-art-direction layouts without custom CSS

name: reveal.js
best_for: Web-native presentations with plugins, fragments, and flexible layout
risk: Browser presentation is not a native editable PPTX

name: Quarto
best_for: Reproducible reports, books, sites, and presentations mixing code and narrative
risk: Scientific publishing defaults still need audience-specific art direction

name: Typst
best_for: Fast programmable high-quality typesetting and PDF documents
risk: PPTX editability and office-template workflows need a different tool

name: Pandoc
license_hint: GPL-2.0; inspect current COPYING for any later-version option
best_for: Document format conversion and structured publishing pipelines
risk: Conversion preserves structure better than visual fidelity; always reverse-review output

name: python-pptx
best_for: Python-based PPTX inspection and native element manipulation
risk: Does not provide art direction or complete PowerPoint feature parity

name: LibreOffice
license_hint: MPL-2.0/LGPL-3.0-or-later dual framework; GitHub API currently classifies GPL-3.0; inspect COPYING
best_for: Headless office conversion, compatibility checks, and document rendering
risk: Rendering differs from Microsoft Office; report the viewer actually tested

name: diagrams.net
best_for: Mature editable technical and business diagrams
risk: Large symbol libraries can encourage generic architecture diagrams

name: D2
best_for: Text-defined diagrams with multiple layouts and reproducible source
risk: Auto-layout must be art-directed and manually reviewed at final scale

name: Mermaid
best_for: Portable text-defined common diagrams embedded in docs and apps
risk: Complex diagrams and premium editorial composition often exceed its layout control

name: ImageMagick
best_for: Broad batch raster conversion, composition, color, and metadata operations
risk: Command availability and delegates vary; verify exact output and security policy

name: libvips
license_hint: LGPL-2.1; inspect current COPYING for any later-version option
best_for: Fast memory-efficient large-image processing
risk: Low-level pipeline; visual quality still requires explicit crop/color decisions

name: Sharp
best_for: Production Node image resizing, formats, compression, and responsive assets
risk: Optimization can destroy text/edge quality if acceptance thresholds are absent

name: SVGO
best_for: SVG cleanup and size optimization
risk: Aggressive plugins can alter IDs, viewBoxes, accessibility, or animation hooks

name: rembg
best_for: Local background removal and batch cutouts
risk: Hair, transparent materials, shadows, and product edges need human inspection

name: Style Dictionary
best_for: Transforming design tokens across web, native, and multiple formats
risk: Token machinery cannot decide the design rationale or semantic naming

name: Kdenlive
license_hint: GPL-3.0; inspect current COPYING for any later-version option
best_for: Mature desktop multitrack editing and human finishing
risk: Automation and exact project portability require canaries on the target platform

name: Shotcut
best_for: Cross-platform desktop editing and broad media format support
risk: Manual timeline ownership is different from deterministic agent automation

name: Palmier Pro
best_for: AI-operable native timeline finishing through MCP
risk: Validate the actual version and MCP canary; do not confuse mechanical edits with direction

name: Remotion
license_hint: Custom entity-size license; inspect current terms
best_for: React timeline composition, deterministic video, overlays, and frame-level tests
risk: License depends on legal entity; a custom React timeline still requires editorial direction

name: Motion Canvas
best_for: TypeScript canvas animation and explanatory motion graphics
risk: Not a general-purpose footage NLE; complex editing and audio workflows need other layers

name: Revideo
best_for: Programmatic TypeScript video editing and template-driven composition
risk: Verify API/repository identity and maturity before production adoption

name: FFmpeg
best_for: Encoding, decoding, filtering, probing, packaging, and final media verification
risk: A filter graph is not an editorial timeline; build configuration changes license obligations

name: Playwright
best_for: Deterministic real-browser product capture and interaction telemetry
risk: Raw automation footage is a truth source, not a finished product film

name: Whisper
best_for: Local multilingual speech recognition and caption timing baseline
risk: Names, numerals, jargon, and final caption rhythm require human correction

name: Audacity
best_for: Waveform editing, cleanup, measurement, and accessible manual audio repair
risk: Effects cannot repair a bad voice identity or missing usage rights

name: Blender
best_for: Full 3D modeling, animation, compositing, simulation, rendering, and scripting
risk: Mature software does not make primitive geometry or stock materials authored design

name: Manim Community
best_for: Mathematical, algorithmic, and structured explanatory animation
risk: Do not force its visual grammar onto product films or emotional campaigns

name: OpenToonz
best_for: Traditional 2D animation, scanning, cleanup, effects, and exposure sheets
risk: Third-party assets/components have separate terms and the workflow is not agent-native

name: ComfyUI
best_for: Node-based reproducible image, video, and audio generation workflows
risk: Models, custom nodes, and outputs have separate licenses; generation is not evidence

name: openFrameworks
best_for: C++ realtime creative coding, installations, sensing, and audiovisual systems
risk: Higher engineering cost than web tools; use only when realtime/native needs justify it

name: AudioCraft
license_hint: MIT code; model weights and datasets have separate terms
best_for: Research and prototyping for music and sound generation
risk: Code license does not grant commercial rights to every model or generated asset

name: Godot Engine
best_for: Open-source 2D/3D game production with an integrated scene, UI, animation, and scripting stack
risk: Engine capability does not replace authored HUD, interaction, asset, performance, and export decisions

name: Bevy
license_hint: Dual MIT OR Apache-2.0; GitHub currently reports Apache-2.0
best_for: Code-first Rust games, ECS architecture, rendering, and custom runtime interaction systems
risk: Dual-license choice and a code-first editor-light workflow require explicit adoption and production review

name: Cocos Creator Engine
license_hint: Repository LICENSE is MIT; GitHub reports NOASSERTION
best_for: Cross-platform 2D/3D games and UI-heavy mobile or web game production
risk: Creator tooling, services, dependencies, and deployment targets may carry terms beyond the engine repository

name: GDevelop
license_hint: Core, engine, IDE, and extensions are MIT; name and logo are reserved; GitHub reports NOASSERTION
best_for: Visual-event authoring, rapid 2D game prototypes, educational projects, and lightweight cross-platform delivery
risk: Trademark, hosted-service, asset-store, extension, and export terms must be separated from core-code licensing

name: Defold
license_hint: Custom Defold License 1.0; source available but not a standard SPDX license
best_for: Compact Lua-driven 2D games, deterministic builds, mobile, desktop, console, and web targets
risk: Do not label it standard OSI open source; review custom license and platform/export terms before adoption

name: Pixelorama
best_for: Pixel-art sprites, frame animation, tiles, palettes, and game-ready raster asset editing
risk: A sprite editor cannot decide silhouette, animation timing, readability, or engine import contracts

name: LibreSprite
best_for: Desktop pixel-art and sprite animation workflows compatible with mature frame-based editing conventions
risk: Copyleft obligations apply to software modification/distribution; shipped art provenance remains a separate review

name: Penpot
best_for: Open design and prototyping workflows using web standards, components, layouts, and team collaboration
risk: Its component model and defaults still require a deliberate product system and export/handoff validation

name: Graphite
best_for: Web-native vector illustration and node-based procedural graphic workflows
risk: Confirm feature maturity, file compatibility, typography, color, and export fidelity before production adoption

name: SVG-Edit
best_for: Embeddable browser-based SVG editing and direct vector document manipulation
risk: It is a focused editor foundation, not a complete illustration, brand, typography, or asset-management system

name: Krita
best_for: Digital painting, illustration, concept art, texture work, brushes, and frame animation
risk: Brush packs, fonts, source references, and imported assets have their own rights and provenance requirements

name: GIMP
license_hint: GPL family with component and plug-in nuances; GitHub mirror reports NOASSERTION
best_for: Raster editing, retouching, compositing, masks, color adjustment, and scriptable image workflows
risk: Official development is on GNOME GitLab; component, plug-in, bundled asset, and distribution terms need review

name: darktable
best_for: Non-destructive RAW photography, color-managed development, cataloging, and batch export
risk: Camera profiles, display calibration, sidecars, export color space, and target-viewer checks are essential

name: RawTherapee
best_for: High-control RAW development, demosaicing, color, noise, lens correction, and batch output
risk: Complex controls can produce technically processed but visually inconsistent sets without an authored color baseline

name: Storybook
best_for: Isolated component states, interaction proofs, visual review, documentation, and design-system regression evidence
risk: A component workbench is not product information architecture or art direction; production parity and accessibility still need explicit gates

name: axe-core
best_for: Automated accessibility rules embedded in browser, component, and CI workflows
risk: Automated checks cover only detectable rules; keyboard, screen-reader, cognitive, motion, and content review remain manual

name: Pa11y
best_for: Repeatable command-line and CI accessibility audits across real pages and journeys
risk: Rule output must be triaged against the real user flow and does not replace assistive-technology testing

name: reg-suit
best_for: Snapshot comparison and review workflows for stable visual baselines
risk: Pixel diffs can be noisy or blind to semantic breakage; freeze fonts, browser, data, viewport, animation, and approved baselines

name: Iconify
license_hint: MIT core; individual icon collections retain separate licenses and trademark constraints
best_for: Unified icon data, rendering, optimization, and framework integration across many icon sets
risk: The core license does not grant uniform rights to every icon collection; choose one coherent family and record per-set attribution/trademark terms

name: FontTools
best_for: Font inspection, subsetting, conversion, variable-font operations, and reproducible typography pipelines
risk: Tool licensing does not grant font embedding or redistribution rights; preserve the selected typeface license and glyph coverage

name: OBS Studio
best_for: Deterministic desktop, camera, source, and audio capture with reusable scene layouts
risk: Capture setup is not editorial direction; plugins, codecs, fonts, overlays, privacy, and platform-specific sources need separate review

name: Subtitle Edit
best_for: Subtitle timing, waveform review, format conversion, OCR cleanup, and caption QA
risk: Automatic transcription and translation require human language, reading-speed, line-break, speaker, and export-format review

name: Natron
best_for: Node-based 2D compositing, keying, tracking, masks, transforms, and repeatable finishing graphs
risk: Plug-ins, codecs, OpenFX components, color management, and distribution may have separate terms; compositing cannot hide product defects

name: Synfig Studio
best_for: Vector tweening, cutout rigs, reusable animation systems, and longer-form 2D production
risk: A capable timeline does not define the visual language; asset provenance, rig quality, interpolation, and export color/fps need review

name: Pencil2D
best_for: Lightweight hand-drawn raster/vector animation, roughs, timing tests, and frame-by-frame studies
risk: Limited pipeline depth compared with larger animation systems; finishing, audio, compositing, and delivery may need external tools

name: OpenColorIO
best_for: Consistent scene/display color transforms across image, video, VFX, and 3D applications
risk: A configuration must match the actual camera, render, display, and delivery target; bundled configs and LUTs have separate provenance

name: OpenImageIO
best_for: Production image I/O, metadata, texture, color, diff, and batch-processing pipelines
risk: Format support and command-line power are execution mechanics; preserve source truth, alpha, bit depth, color space, and deterministic manifests

name: Material Maker
best_for: Procedural PBR materials, texture generation, and Godot-oriented shader workflows
risk: Procedural nodes do not create an authored material world by themselves; test scale, seams, channels, engine import, and asset rights

name: glTF-Transform
best_for: Inspecting, transforming, optimizing, compressing, and validating glTF assets in reproducible pipelines
risk: Optimization can damage geometry, materials, animation, accessibility metadata, or visual baselines; compare before and after in the target renderer

name: MeshLab
best_for: Mesh inspection, cleanup, simplification, measurement, reconstruction, and scanned-asset repair
risk: Destructive filters need reversible source copies and visual/geometric regression checks; it is not a scene, rig, material, or art-direction tool

name: Inkscape
license_hint: GPL family; inspect current COPYING and extension/asset terms
best_for: Mature desktop SVG illustration, typography, path editing, print assets, and interoperable vector production
risk: GitLab metadata does not provide a reliable live SPDX or archived field; extensions, fonts, linked media, profiles, and final export require separate review

name: Scribus
license_hint: GPL family; inspect current COPYING and bundled component terms
best_for: Page layout, print production, PDF prepress, color-managed publishing, and editable long-form collateral
risk: GitLab metadata does not provide reliable live SPDX or archived fields; fonts, linked images, bleed, profiles, print standards, and output intent need QA

name: Ardour
license_hint: GPL family with bundled libraries and plug-in boundaries; GitHub reports NOASSERTION
best_for: Multitrack editing, mixing, automation, routing, loudness, and professional audio finishing
risk: Plug-ins, codecs, sample libraries, distribution, and third-party binaries have separate terms; mastering cannot repair weak recording or inconsistent speech identity

name: Processing
license_hint: Multi-file GPL/LGPL and library terms; GitHub reports NOASSERTION
best_for: Desktop creative coding, interactive installations, data-driven art, sketches, and education
risk: Core, libraries, assets, and exported applications may have different terms; procedural output must follow an authored concept and accessibility plan

name: Cinder
license_hint: Custom/BSD-style multi-component terms; GitHub reports NOASSERTION
best_for: High-performance C++ creative coding, installations, graphics, camera, audio, and hardware integration
risk: Framework, blocks, codecs, assets, platform SDKs, and distribution need separate review; engineering complexity is unjustified for decorative filler

name: Lottie Web
best_for: Rendering authored After Effects/Lottie vector animation data in web products with compact reusable assets
risk: A runtime is not an animation authoring system; exported JSON, fonts, images, expressions, accessibility, reduced motion, and asset rights need review

name: OpenTimelineIO
best_for: Interchanging editorial timelines, clips, ranges, transitions, and metadata between supported production tools
risk: Interchange preserves only supported semantics; effects, color, speed, media relinking, plug-ins, and final render fidelity require target-tool canaries

name: OpenRV
best_for: Professional sequence playback, comparison, annotation, color-aware review, and VFX/media inspection
risk: Repository, bundled components, codecs, plug-ins, and distribution require review; playback approval does not replace target-platform decode and final-user QA
